exposure: maternal glycated albumin levels during late pregnancy
outcome: maternal complications (e.g., cesarean section due to cephalopelvic disproportion)
neonatal complications (e.g., macrosomia, overweight, NICU admission)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 120 singleton pregnant women diagnosed with gestational diabetes who visited Trinium Woman's Hospital between July 1, 2020, and June 30, 2022.
finding: The third trimester glycated albumin test in mothers with gestational diabetes provides limited predictive value for maternal and neonatal complications, despite higher levels being associated with complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the most common maternal complication, occurring in 39 patients due to fetal cephalopelvic disproportion.
